references.text: God blessed them and said to them, 'Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and subdue it!' This is a direct parallel to God's blessing and command to Noah and his sons, representing a reestablishment of humanity's mission on earth after the flood.
'Be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth and multiply in it.' This verse repeats the command given in verse 1, emphasizing the importance of humanity's spread and growth after the flood.

God commands that all living creatures shall come out of the ark to 'swarm on the earth, be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.' This is the immediate context before God's blessing of Noah in Gen 9:1.
God said to Jacob, 'Be fruitful and multiply!' This blessing to Jacob repeats the same language as in God's blessing of Noah, showing continuity in God's plan for humanity through the patriarchs.
Restoration of the creation order: God's blessing to Noah mirrors the original blessing given to Adam, marking a new starting point of creation for humanity.
Historical fulfillment: The verses in Psalms show that God's command to Noah (and Abraham) to become numerous was fulfilled in Israel's history.
Clear contrast: The judgment on the corrupt world (Gen 6:13) and the immediate restoration and new call to humanity (Gen 9:1).
Development of the covenant: Noah's blessing of all humanity is a precursor to Abraham's covenant that all families shall be blessed.
Historical fulfillment: Israel's explosive growth in Egypt is a direct fulfillment of God's command to be fruitful and multiply.
Contrast between rescue and new beginning: Entering the ark to survive judgment (Gen 7:1) is the prerequisite for going out and filling the earth (Gen 9:1).
